name: Welcome Ride
description: Become comfortable riding at an easy effort.

name: Pedal Smoothly
description: Introduce smooth changes in leg speed without increasing effort significantly.

name: First Endurance Ride
description: Complete a longer continuous ride at a comfortable pace.

name: Easy Foundation Ride
description: Relaxed posture, quiet upper body and sustainable effort.

name: Cadence Introduction
description: Change leg speed while keeping the effort controlled.

name: Comfortable Endurance Ride
description: Extend riding time without rushing the pace. The final block should feel like the first.

name: Steady Foundation Ride
description: Recognise a small, sustainable change in effort. Steady riding should feel purposeful but controlled — you can still speak in short sentences.

name: Rhythm Changes
description: Change rhythm several times and return to control after each effort.

name: Endurance Builder
description: Reach 40 minutes by keeping the ride patient and controlled — manage your energy.

name: Easy Reset Ride
description: Relaxed posture, light resistance and smooth breathing.

name: Smooth Pedalling Skills
description: Quiet hips, relaxed ankles, light hands and consistent pressure through the pedals.

name: Comfortable Endurance Ride
description: Finish the ride feeling that another five minutes would have been possible.

name: Aerobic Foundation Ride
description: Build comfortable aerobic endurance — finish exercised but not drained.

name: Steady Steps
description: Introduce short moderate blocks while maintaining form and breathing.

name: Endurance Ride
description: Extend continuous riding time at a controlled pace. The first block should feel easier than the last.

name: Steady Endurance Ride
description: Sustain a steady aerobic rhythm for longer. The second steady block should match the first.

name: Cadence and Control
description: Increase cadence while maintaining posture and controlled breathing.

name: Longer Endurance Ride
description: Ride for 50 minutes with comfortable pacing — feel capable of another five minutes at the end.

name: Easy Start, Strong Finish
description: Practise pacing — begin easily and finish at a controlled steady effort. Do not jump from easy to moderate.

name: Controlled Effort Blocks
description: Repeat moderate efforts without losing technique. Steady blocks 72–85 rpm, recovery 60–75 rpm.

name: Paced Endurance Ride
description: Longest ride of Phase 2. Do not exceed RPE 3 during the first 20 minutes of endurance work.

name: Recovery Spin
description: Promote circulation and reinforce relaxed technique. Use the lightest resistance that still allows smooth pedalling.

name: Smooth and Efficient
description: Reinforce smooth cadence and relaxed posture. Keep hips quiet, ankles relaxed, hands light; avoid a heavy gear.

name: Comfortable Endurance Ride
description: Finish feeling that another five to ten minutes would have been possible.

name: Aerobic Foundation Ride
description: Reinforce aerobic endurance before introducing hill work — a calm rhythm that prepares you for Thursday.

name: Gentle Rolling Hills
description: Respond to gentle terrain by shifting early, adding manageable resistance and keeping a smooth seated cadence.

name: Endurance Builder
description: Extend continuous riding with good posture and pacing. First 20 minutes easy enough to speak comfortably.

name: Steady Foundation Ride
description: Hold steady aerobic riding for longer without drifting into excessive effort. Second steady block matches the first.

name: Cadence and Endurance
description: Combine cadence changes with comfortable endurance. Shift lighter before increasing cadence; keep hips quiet; avoid bouncing.

name: Long Endurance Ride
description: Complete the first controlled 60-minute ride. Keep the first 30 minutes easier than the final 20. Take small drinks regularly.

name: Aerobic Endurance Ride
description: Maintain a continuous aerobic rhythm with a controlled finish — reach it with energy for good posture and cadence.

name: Controlled Steady Blocks
description: Repeat longer steady efforts while maintaining technique. Steady blocks 72–85 rpm, recovery 60–75 rpm.

name: Long Endurance Ride
description: Longest ride of Phase 3. Do not exceed RPE 3 during the first 32 minutes. Take a small familiar carb snack if needed — nothing new.

name: Easy Reset Ride
description: Promote recovery while maintaining comfortable movement. Light resistance; finish feeling more mobile than at the start.

name: Technique and Control
description: Reinforce smooth cadence, early shifting and relaxed posture. Shift before cadence becomes heavy; stay seated; hips quiet.

name: Comfortable Endurance Ride
description: Finish with energy in reserve. The final block should feel as controlled as the first.

name: Steady Foundation Ride
description: Reinforce steady aerobic control before the longer weekend ride — finish with energy for the rest of the week.

name: Cadence and Gentle Hills
description: Combine smooth cadence with gentle resistance and hill management — move between flat cadence work and controlled seated climbing without abrupt changes.

name: Long Endurance Ride
description: Become comfortable riding beyond one hour. Do not exceed RPE 3 during the first 42 minutes.

name: Aerobic Endurance Ride
description: Maintain continuous aerobic work with a controlled progressive finish. Build the effort gradually rather than jumping straight to the finish.

name: Controlled Endurance Intervals
description: Complete longer controlled efforts without drifting into high intensity — sustain moderate effort, recover and repeat while maintaining posture and breathing control.

name: Long Endurance Ride
description: Complete 80 minutes while maintaining sustainable pacing and good technique. Feel deliberately restrained during the first 30 minutes.

name: Steady and Strong
description: Begin conservatively and finish with controlled strength. The final four minutes should feel strong but never desperate.

name: Pacing, Cadence and Hills
description: Combine easy endurance, cadence control, gentle seated climbing and pacing. Transition smoothly between each type of effort.

name: Longest Training Ride
description: Complete the longest training ride before achievement week. Practise patient pacing, hydration, fuelling, posture and fatigue management. The first 48 minutes must remain easy and controlled. This is not the final achievement ride.

name: Confidence Ride
description: Reinforce confidence and comfortable movement without creating fatigue. Nothing new is required — trust the skills you have built.

name: Leg Opener and Skills Ride
description: Keep the legs responsive while avoiding fatigue before the achievement ride. The cadence efforts should make the legs feel responsive, not tired.

name: From Couch to Road Achievement Ride
description: Bring together sixteen weeks of endurance, pacing, cadence and confidence. Not a pass-or-fail test. Choose Full (90 min), Supported (75 min) or Foundation (60 min) — completing any option counts as completing the plan.

name: Intermediate Baseline Ride
description: Establish your current sustainable effort, cadence control and recovery response.

name: Cadence and Aerobic Control
description: Improve cadence awareness while maintaining a stable aerobic effort.

name: Foundation Endurance Ride
description: Complete a controlled 90-minute ride, establishing sustainable pacing, hydration and posture habits.

name: Tempo Introduction
description: Complete three repeatable tempo efforts without drifting into threshold intensity.

name: Aerobic Endurance and Cadence Changes
description: Maintain endurance effort while moving smoothly between different cadence ranges.

name: Progressive Endurance Ride
description: Complete a progressively paced endurance ride without starting too strongly.

name: Sustained Tempo
description: Sustain two longer tempo intervals with stable pacing and technique.

name: Seated Strength and Control
description: Develop controlled cycling strength using moderate resistance and a smooth seated cadence.

name: Long Aerobic Durability Ride
description: Complete the longest ride of Phase 1 while maintaining sustainable energy, posture and cadence.

name: Controlled Aerobic Reassessment
description: Compare aerobic comfort, cadence and moderate effort with the Week 1 baseline ride.

name: Skills Consolidation Ride
description: Rehearse the main Phase 1 skills without creating fatigue.

name: Phase 1 Confidence Ride
description: Complete Phase 1 with a controlled endurance ride that reinforces confidence and recovery.

name: Tempo Strength Builder
description: Complete three controlled tempo intervals while maintaining stable cadence and posture.

name: Cadence Under Load
description: Maintain smooth cadence as resistance changes.

name: Long Steady Endurance Ride
description: Extend aerobic endurance while practising steady fuelling and posture management.

name: Seated Climbing Strength
description: Complete repeated controlled seated climbing intervals without grinding.

name: Aerobic Endurance with Hill Skills
description: Maintain aerobic control while responding smoothly to gentle changes in terrain or resistance.

name: Hills and Endurance
description: Complete a longer endurance ride that includes controlled rolling terrain or simulated hills.

name: Controlled Threshold Development
description: Complete three controlled harder efforts without entering maximal intensity.

name: Aerobic Maintenance
description: Maintain aerobic conditioning without adding excessive fatigue after Tuesday's harder session.

name: Goal-Specific Durability Ride
description: Maintain useful goal-related effort during the second half of a two-hour ride. Endurance first, goal-specific work second.

name: Short Tempo Consolidation
description: Reinforce controlled tempo without adding significant fatigue.

name: Strength and Cadence Consolidation
description: Rehearse seated strength, cadence and recovery without creating fatigue.

name: Phase 2 Confidence Endurance Ride
description: Complete Phase 2 with a controlled ride that confirms improved strength, pacing and endurance.

name: Goal-Specific Intervals
description: Complete controlled intervals that directly support your selected current goal.

name: Aerobic Endurance and Leg Speed
description: Maintain aerobic fitness while keeping cadence responsive after Tuesday's goal-specific work.

name: Goal Simulation Ride
description: Practise the pacing, terrain, hydration and fuelling requirements of your goal.

name: Sustained Goal Effort
description: Complete two longer goal-specific intervals with stable pacing and technique.

name: Endurance with Leg Openers
description: Maintain endurance while completing brief controlled efforts that keep the legs responsive.

name: Peak Goal-Specific Training Ride
description: Complete the most demanding goal-specific training ride before achievement preparation begins.

name: Controlled Sharpening
description: Maintain high-quality goal-specific effort with reduced interval duration.

name: Steady Endurance and Technique
description: Maintain endurance while reinforcing relaxed technique and efficient pacing.

name: Achievement Confidence Simulation
description: Rehearse the achievement ride strategy at a reduced duration and controlled intensity.

name: Achievement Confidence Ride
description: Reinforce comfortable movement and confidence without creating fatigue.

name: Leg Opener and Goal Skills Ride
description: Keep the legs responsive and rehearse one final goal-specific skill without creating fatigue.

name: Ride Stronger Achievement Ride
description: Demonstrate the endurance, strength, pacing and confidence built across twelve weeks. Choose Full (150 min), Supported (120 min) or Foundation (90 min) — any approved option completes Ride Stronger. Not a pass/fail test.

name: Advanced Performance Baseline
description: Establish your current aerobic, sustained-power and high-intensity baseline.

name: Cadence Range and Aerobic Control
description: Maintain smooth power while changing cadence — stay efficient across pedalling speeds.

name: Advanced Foundation Endurance Ride
description: Build the aerobic endurance required for advanced training; finish as strong as you started.

name: Sustained Tempo Development
description: Sustain a strong pace below threshold — demanding enough to adapt, controlled enough to repeat.

name: Aerobic Endurance with Cadence Changes
description: Stay aerobically stable while cadence and resistance change — efficiency for rolling roads and wind.

name: Progressive Endurance Ride
description: Build intensity gradually across a long ride — finish stronger than you began, without losing control.

name: Controlled Threshold Development
description: Sustain a demanding effort near threshold — every interval consistent, never over-cooked on the first.

name: Seated Climbing Strength and Control
description: Develop the force for sustained climbing while reinforcing controlled pedalling technique.

name: Hills and Endurance
description: Combine aerobic endurance with sustained climbing — controlled power while managing a long ride.

name: Tempo and Threshold Consolidation
description: Hold intensity with less total work — sharp, clean, energy remaining at the end.

name: Aerobic Maintenance and Technique
description: Easy aerobic maintenance with light, smooth high-cadence work — finish better than you started.

name: Phase 1 Confidence Endurance Ride
description: Bring together endurance, tempo, threshold, cadence and fuelling — confirm your strength is repeatable.

name: Advanced Tempo Strength Builder
focus: Sustainable Tempo Power and Muscular Endurance
description: Build the strength to create sustained pressure — and the control to hold it.

name: Cadence Under Load
focus: Maintaining Power through Cadence and Resistance Changes
description: Hold the same calm control as cadence and resistance change beneath you.

name: Long Steady Endurance Ride
description: Build aerobic durability one controlled hour at a time; practise your goal-ride fuelling.

name: Seated Climbing Strength
description: Build climbing power that begins with control and finishes with confidence.

name: Aerobic Endurance with Hill Skills
description: Stand with purpose, sit with control, and keep the climb flowing through every transition.

name: Hills and Endurance
description: Respect every ascent, recover for the next, and build durable climbing endurance.

name: Threshold Progression
description: Threshold power matters most when you can repeat it — hold each effort evenly.

name: VO₂ Power Intervals
description: Keep the final interval looking like cycling — quality across the whole set, not survival.

name: Goal-Specific Durability Ride
description: Late-ride strength is prepared long before the final interval begins.

name: Short Tempo Consolidation
focus: Tempo Maintenance and Short High-Intensity Activation
description: Keep the engine awake without draining the tank.

name: Strength and Cadence Consolidation
focus: Maintaining Climbing Strength and Cadence Range
description: Turn hard-earned fitness into dependable performance.

name: Phase 2 Confidence Endurance Ride
description: Confirm you can still produce quality after the easy kilometres are gone.

name: Goal-Specific Over-Under Intervals
focus: Threshold Control and Changes of Pace
description: Control the surge, settle back into strength and keep moving forward.

name: Aerobic Endurance and Leg Speed
description: Fast legs should feel light and precise — not rushed.

name: Goal Simulation Ride
description: Simulation turns preparation into confidence.

name: Sustained Goal Effort
description: Train the performance your goal will ask you to deliver.

name: Endurance with Leg Openers
description: Open the legs, wake up the power and save the best work for the weekend.

name: Peak Goal-Specific Training Ride
description: Your peak ride should prove your preparation — not empty everything you have.

name: Controlled Sharpening
description: Sharpness comes from quality — not from squeezing in more fatigue.

name: Steady Endurance and Technique
description: Confidence grows when the simple things become smooth and automatic.

name: Achievement Confidence Simulation
description: You do not need to prove your fitness today. You only need to trust it.

name: Achievement Confidence Ride
description: Confidence is knowing you could do more — and choosing to save it.

name: Leg Opener and Goal Skills Ride
description: Wake up the legs, settle the mind and leave the rest for Achievement Day.

name: Ride Beyond Achievement Ride
description: Complete a meaningful advanced challenge with control, confidence and intelligent pacing.

name: Aerobic Base
description: A gentle, steady Zone 2 introduction to build your aerobic engine. Stay comfortable and conversational throughout.

name: Aerobic Base
description: Two solid Zone 2 blocks with an easy spin between. Builds aerobic efficiency without accumulating fatigue.

name: Aerobic Base
description: Three upper Zone 2 blocks to deepen aerobic durability. Hold a strong, even effort just below tempo.

name: Endurance Progression
description: A gradual build from easy to steady Zone 2. Finish strong — never let it drift into a threshold effort.

name: Endurance Progression
description: Step up through the Zone 2 range and finish in upper Zone 2. Keep the progression smooth and controlled.

name: Endurance Progression
description: A full progression finishing with a short controlled tempo touch. Strong to the line, but never breathless.

name: Aerobic Endurance Intervals
description: Short, repeatable Zone 2 intervals with easy spins between. A friendly first step into structured endurance work.

name: Aerobic Endurance Intervals
description: Three upper Zone 2 intervals to extend aerobic endurance. Hold each effort steady and even.

name: Aerobic Endurance Intervals
description: Three long upper Zone 2 intervals for serious aerobic durability. Strong, sustainable and controlled.

name: Tempo Endurance Builder
description: A first taste of tempo — two short low-tempo efforts. Strong but sustainable, never breathless or competitive.

name: Tempo Endurance Builder
description: Two ten-minute tempo blocks to build muscular endurance. Hold a strong, even effort — controlled, not competitive.

name: Tempo Endurance Builder
description: Three ten-minute tempo efforts for durable, sustainable power. Strong and steady — keep it well short of threshold.

name: Strength Endurance
description: Short low-cadence efforts (70–75 rpm) to build muscular strength. 50+ tip: use a comfortable resistance — never heavy-gear grinding — and back off if your knees, hips or lower back complain. A seated version works well.

name: Strength Endurance
description: Four-minute low-cadence blocks (65–75 rpm) for muscular endurance. 50+ tip: keep it smooth and controlled, not a grind — reduce resistance the moment a joint feels uncomfortable. Seated version optional.

name: Strength Endurance
description: Five four-minute blocks at 60–70 rpm for real muscular durability. 50+ tip: this should never become heavy-gear grinding — protect your knees, hips and back with lighter resistance and a more natural cadence if needed.

name: Indoor Endurance Durability
description: Steady Zone 2 blocks that build durability without the marathon time cost. 50+ tip: change hand position and posture regularly, and keep it comfortable throughout.

name: Indoor Endurance Durability
description: Three ten-minute Zone 2 blocks, each with a one-minute higher-cadence lift to keep the legs lively. 50+ tip: shift hand position and cadence often, and ease resistance if anything feels uncomfortable.

name: Indoor Endurance Durability
description: Three long Zone 2 blocks that each finish in upper Zone 2 — durable endurance in 70 focused minutes. 50+ tip: keep the finishes controlled, vary your position, and reduce resistance any time joints feel it.

name: Threshold Intervals
description: A gentle introduction to threshold work — two short efforts just below your limit. 50+ tip: keep your breathing controlled and ease off early if your form starts to fade.

name: Threshold Intervals
description: Three eight-minute efforts right at threshold to lift your sustainable power. Hold a strong, even cadence and repeatable output across all three.

name: Threshold Intervals
description: Four demanding eight-minute threshold efforts for serious FTP gains. Precise pacing throughout — every effort should look the same on power.

name: VO2 Max Intervals
description: Short two-minute efforts to open up your top-end aerobic system. 50+ tip: build into each rep rather than starting flat-out, and stop if you feel light-headed.

name: VO2 Max Intervals
description: Classic five-by-three-minute VO2 efforts with equal recovery. Raises your aerobic ceiling and the power you can hold when it really hurts.

name: VO2 Max Intervals
description: Six brutal three-minute VO2 efforts for the strongest riders. Hold your target on every rep — this is where race-winning fitness is built.

name: Sprint Power
description: Five short fifteen-second sprints with full recovery. 50+ tip: stay seated or rise smoothly — never lunge — and keep plenty of easy spinning between efforts.

name: Sprint Power
description: Six maximal fifteen-second sprints to sharpen your top-end speed and neuromuscular power. Full, unhurried recovery between each.

name: Sprint Power
description: Eight all-out sprints for a race-winning kick. Commit fully to each effort, then recover completely — quality over quantity every time.

name: Recovery Spin
description: A short, feather-light spin to promote blood flow and ease the legs. Keep it gentle and high-cadence — this should feel restful, not like training.

name: Recovery Spin
description: An easy thirty-five-minute flush to speed recovery between harder days. Stay strictly in Zone 1 and enjoy the spin.

name: Recovery Spin
description: A longer active-recovery spin with a couple of light cadence lifts to keep the legs supple. Still easy throughout — recovery is the goal, not fitness.

name: Endurance Ride
description: A long, steady Zone 2 ride to build your aerobic engine and fat-burning efficiency. Keep it conversational the whole way. Best done outdoors where terrain and momentum keep it engaging.

name: Long Base Builder
description: Extended endurance ride with a few tempo surges to keep the legs honest. Great weekend base session — take it outdoors for the full experience.

name: Fasted Aerobic Spin
description: Gentle, controlled aerobic ride to develop metabolic efficiency. Stay strictly in Zone 2.

name: Threshold Climb
description: Long sustained climbing efforts at threshold to build the power you need on real mountains. Hold a strong, even cadence.

name: Hill Repeats
description: Repeated hard climbs with recovery descents. Builds muscular endurance and the ability to attack gradients.

name: Alpine Simulator
description: A long climb simulation blending tempo and threshold to prepare for grand-tour style ascents. An outdoor big-mountain day.

name: Sweet Spot 2x20
description: Two 20-minute blocks at 88–94% FTP — the most time-efficient way to raise your threshold without excessive fatigue.

name: FTP Intervals 4x8
description: Four 8-minute efforts just above threshold. Tough but hugely effective for lifting your sustainable power.

name: Over-Unders
description: Alternating efforts above and below threshold to train your body to clear lactate while still working hard.

name: VO2 Max Intervals
description: Classic 5x3-minute efforts at VO2 max with equal recovery. Raises your aerobic ceiling and top-end sustainable power.

name: 30/30 Bursts
description: Alternating 30s hard / 30s easy microbursts. Builds the ability to repeat high-intensity efforts.

name: Peak Power Sprints
description: Maximal 15-second sprints with full recovery. Develops neuromuscular power and top-end speed.

name: Criterium Simulator
description: Repeated hard accelerations out of corners followed by surging efforts — just like a crit finish.

name: Tempo Endurance
description: Sustained Zone 3 riding to build muscular endurance and the ability to hold a strong steady pace.

name: Time Trial Simulator
description: A steady, disciplined effort blending tempo and threshold to sharpen your pacing for time trials.

name: Recovery Spin
description: Very light, high-cadence spinning to promote blood flow and speed up recovery between hard days.

name: Easy Flush Ride
description: A short, gentle flush to loosen the legs and reduce fatigue. Keep it feather-light.

name: Full Rest Day
description: Planned complete rest so your body can adapt and grow stronger. Hydrate, eat well and sleep.

name: FB50 Glute Activation
description: Targeted glute and hip activation to fire the right muscles before you ride, improving power transfer and protecting your knees.

name: FB50 Core & Stability
description: Cyclist-focused core and stability work to hold a stronger, more efficient position on the bike for longer.

name: FB50 Post-Ride Mobility
description: Gentle mobility and stretching to release tight hips, hamstrings and back after riding, aiding recovery.
